text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 3 in history.
1226 - St Francis of Assisi, founder of the Franciscan order, died.
1656 - Myles Standish, one of the Pilgrim Fathers who sailed in the Mayflower, died aged about 72.
1691 - The Treaty of Limerick was signed, ending the Irish Rebellion.
1859 - Eleonora Duse, Italian actress, born. Famous worldwide for her interpretations of the heroines of Henrik Ibsen.
1863 - U.S. President Abraham Lincoln issued a proclamation designating the last Thursday in November as Thanksgiving Day.
1888 - Carl von Ossietzky, German journalist, born. In 1935 he won the Nobel Peace Prize for his exposure of Nazi rearmament before World War Two.
1896 - William Morris, English craftsman, poet and painter, died aged 62.

1897 - Louis Aragon, French poet, essayist and novelist, born. He was a founder of the Surrealist and Dadaist movements which flourished in Paris in the first half of the 20th century. He was also a major figure in the French resistance.
1906 - SOS was established as an international distress signal at the Berlin Radio Conference.
1911 - Sir Michael Hordern born. An English character actor of stage and screen who also played many Shakesperian roles, his film credits include "Bed-Sitting Room" and "Anne of a Thousand Days".
1916 - James Herriott (James Alfred Wight) born. British author and vet who wrote a series of novels based on the experiences of a Yorkshire vet, including "All Creatures Great and Small".
1928 - Kaare Willoch, Norwegian Prime Minister 1981-86, born.
1929 - Yugoslavia became the official name of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.
1932 - Iraq became independent and joined the League of Nations after the British mandate ended.
1938 - Eddie Cochran, U.S. pop singer, born. Hits included "C'mon Everybody", "Summertime Blues" and "Three Steps to Heaven".
1941 - In a speech Adolf Hitler declared: "Russia is defeated and will never rise again". The German march towards Moscow was subsequently thwarted by the Russian winter.
1941 - Chubby Checker (Ernest Evans) born. U.S. pop singer who popularised "The Twist".
1952 - The first British atomic bomb was detonated at the Monte Bello Islands off north-west Australia.
1963 - A military coup in Honduras overthrew President Ramon Villeda Morales.
1967 - Malcolm Sargent, English conductor noted for his interpretations of Elgar, died.
1976 - Black leader Bishop Abel Muzorewa returned to Rhodesia after two years in exile in Tanzania.
1977 - Former Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was arrested on corruption charges.
1981 - The hunger strike at the Maze prison in Belfast ended after seven months and 10 deaths.
1989 - Troops loyal to Panamanian strongman General Manuel Antonio Noriega crushed a coup attempt by junior officers.
1990 - China and Singapore established diplomatic relations.
1990 - East and West Germany formally united at midnight, burying 45 years of Cold War division.
1990 - Iraqi President Saddam Hussein visited Kuwait, his first known trip to the emirate since his invasion on August 2.
1995 - The O.J. Simpson trial ended with him being cleared of murder charges.
1995 - A car bomb attack injured Macedonia's President Kiro Gligorov and killed his driver.
